cast/people/boniface/life/0: Trained as a scholar of Church law. Worked as a diplomat for the papal court.
cast/people/boniface/life/1: Elected pope in 1294. The pope before him, Celestine V, had stepped down on his own — and at the time there were people in Rome who said Boniface had talked him into it.
cast/people/boniface/life/2: In 1300 he held the first “Jubilee” in Christian history: anyone who came to Rome as a pilgrim was forgiven their sins. People poured into the city from all over Europe. The offerings piled up on the altar of St. Peter's like little hills, and priests stood there raking them in.
cast/people/boniface/life/3: In 1302 he issued Unam Sanctam: anyone who does not obey the pope in Rome cannot be saved. It was the highest claim papal power ever made.
cast/people/boniface/life/4: In 1303, at Anagni, men of King Philip IV of France seized him and humiliated him for three days. A month after they let him go, he died in Rome.
cast/people/boniface/withDante/0: In the autumn of 1301, Florence sent three envoys to Rome to plead its case, and Dante was one of them. He sent the other two home and kept Dante behind.
cast/people/boniface/withDante/1: At the same time, he let Charles of Valois, the French king's brother, march north with troops to “mediate” in Florence. The city opened its own gates. Then came the Blacks' coup, six days of burning and looting, and then that trial.
cast/people/corso_donati/role: Leader of the Blacks, old Florentine noble
cast/people/corso_donati/life/0: Eldest son of the Donati family. Served as chief magistrate of Bologna and of Pistoia.
cast/people/corso_donati/life/1: At Campaldino in 1289 he charged with his cavalry against orders, and won — the credit went on his record, and so did the disobedience.
cast/people/corso_donati/life/2: In 1300 the priors banished him (Dante was one of the priors who signed).
cast/people/corso_donati/life/3: In November 1301 he came back into the city with Charles of Valois and tore the Whites out by the roots. For the next few years he was the man who really ran Florence.
cast/people/corso_donati/life/4: In 1308 his own Blacks accused him of treason. He rode off to escape, Catalan mercenaries caught up with him, and he died on the road outside the city.
cast/people/corso_donati/withDante/0: Dante's wife Gemma was a Donati too — they counted as distant relatives.
cast/people/corso_donati/withDante/1: During the two months Dante was a prior in 1300, his name was on the banishment list. A year later he was back, and the name on the list was Dante's.
cast/people/forese/role: Dante's boyhood friend, Corso's younger brother
cast/people/forese/life/0: Corso's younger brother, Piccarda's older brother. Three of them in one family, and not alike at all.
cast/people/forese/life/1: He never did anything big. He ate too much, loved a good time, and was always short of money.
cast/people/forese/life/2: He died in 1296, six years before Dante's exile — he never saw the great upheaval.
cast/people/forese/withDante/0: When they were young the two of them traded a whole round of insult poems, the really nasty kind: your family is poor, your wife, your coughing in the middle of the night. A set like that is called a tenzone. Both of them kept the poems. Neither destroyed them.
cast/people/forese/withDante/1: When he died, Dante was still in Florence and had not yet gone into politics.
cast/people/beatrice_young/life/0: Her father, Folco Portinari, was one of Florence's great bankers. He paid for the building of the hospital of Santa Maria Nuova.
cast/people/beatrice_young/life/1: She married Simone de' Bardi, of a banking family.
cast/people/beatrice_young/life/2: She died in June 1290, twenty-four years old.
cast/people/beatrice_young/withDante/0: In 1274, when he was nine, he saw her for the first time at a party at her house. She was wearing a crimson dress.
cast/people/beatrice_young/withDante/1: In 1283, when they were both eighteen, she greeted him at the head of the Santa Trinita bridge — Dante wrote: in that moment I seemed to see the very limit of happiness.
cast/people/beatrice_young/withDante/2: In their whole lives they said no more than a few words to each other. After she died, he made a vow at the end of the Vita Nuova: to write about her what no one had ever written about any woman.
cast/people/brunetto/role: Notary, chancellor of the commune, teacher of Florence
cast/people/brunetto/life/0: A Guelph. After the defeat at Montaperti in 1260 he spent six years in exile in France.
cast/people/brunetto/life/1: In France, in French, he wrote the big book of his life, the Trésor — an encyclopedia meant to hold all the learning in the world. His reason: French goes further, more people read it.
cast/people/brunetto/life/2: He also wrote a much shorter verse book in everyday Italian, the Tesoretto. In it the author loses his way in a wood, meets a goddess, and is led on a tour of the reasons behind all things.
cast/people/brunetto/life/3: He came back to the city in 1266 and rose to chancellor of the commune. Villani said he was the one who took the Florentines “from rough to fine” — who taught the city how to speak and how to argue politics.
cast/people/brunetto/withDante/0: We do not actually know how they met: no school record, no contract, not one letter.
cast/people/brunetto/withDante/1: We know there was such a teacher only because Dante later wrote about him.
cast/people/brunetto/withDante/2: What he taught was rhetoric and politics — how to make a whole city understand you. And one line Dante remembered all his life: a man can make himself immortal.
cast/people/piccarda/role: A nun, younger sister of Corso and Forese
cast/people/piccarda/life/0: The youngest child of the Donati family. Corso's sister, Forese's sister.
cast/people/piccarda/life/1: She entered the order of Saint Clare as a nun and took vows for life.
cast/people/piccarda/life/2: For the sake of a political marriage, her brother Corso brought men into the convent, dragged her out, and forced her to marry.
cast/people/piccarda/life/3: She fell ill and died not long after the wedding. Some say she wanted to die — her vow was broken, and she would not go on living with that.
cast/people/piccarda/withDante/0: Dante's wife Gemma was a Donati too, and the two families saw a great deal of each other.
cast/people/piccarda/withDante/1: He knew both her brothers: one was the friend he traded insults with when they were young, the other was the man who drove him out of Florence.
cast/people/cacciaguida/life/0: Born in the old Florence, when the walls were still small. People dressed plainly then, and girls marrying did not compete over dowries.
cast/people/cacciaguida/life/1: He married a woman from the Po valley whose family name was Alighieri — the name was passed down from there, and a hundred years and more later it came to Dante.
cast/people/cacciaguida/life/2: He followed the Emperor Conrad III on the Second Crusade and died fighting in the Holy Land.
cast/people/cacciaguida/withDante/0: He is Dante's great-great-grandfather, four generations back.
cast/people/cacciaguida/withDante/1: In the Paradiso, Dante claims him as his ancestor and has him tell of the old Florence — and say that line about exile: how salty another man's bread is, how steep another man's stairs are.
cast/people/guido_cavalcanti/life/0: 佛罗伦萨最有名的诗人。「温柔新体」那一派，他是领头的那个。
cast/people/guido_cavalcanti/life/1: 父亲卡瓦尔坎特是个出了名不信来世的人——街上都知道他这个说法。
cast/people/guido_cavalcanti/life/2: 娶了法里纳塔·德利·乌贝尔蒂的女儿，一桩把两个死对头家族绑在一起的政治婚姻。
cast/people/guido_cavalcanti/life/3: 脾气很硬。跟科尔索·多纳蒂有私仇，两个人在街上互相动过刀。
cast/people/guido_cavalcanti/life/4: 1300 年 6 月，执政团把两党首恶一起放逐，他被逐往萨尔扎纳——那里瘴气很重。
cast/people/guido_cavalcanti/life/5: 他在那里染上疟疾。当年八月获准回城，回来没几天就死了。
cast/people/guido_cavalcanti/withDante/0: 但丁叫他「第一好友」。《新生》就是写给他的。
cast/people/guido_cavalcanti/withDante/1: 是他把但丁带进那个写诗的圈子。两个人的诗互相引用，来回好些年。
cast/people/guido_cavalcanti/withDante/2: 1300 年那份放逐名单上有他的名字。签字的执政团里，有但丁。
timeline/character/description: Author of the Divine Comedy, the first sign of the European Renaissance, “father of the Italian language”
timeline/stages/0/summary: Dante was born into a minor noble family in Florence. At nine he first saw Beatrice; as a young man he wrote the Vita Nuova. After she died, he turned to books and to a teacher.
timeline/stages/0/events/0/summary: Under the sign of Gemini, a son is born to the Alighieri. The old Florence of his ancestor Cacciaguida — and the first spark of the two parties' quarrel.
timeline/stages/0/events/1/summary: The greeting at the bridge, the battlefield of Campaldino, the death bell of 1290 — and the vow in the last chapter of the Vita Nuova.
timeline/stages/0/events/2/summary: After Beatrice died, he buried himself in books. The most learned old man in the city taught him rhetoric, politics, and one line he did not understand yet.
timeline/stages/0/events/2/comedyAnchor/: Sand under rain of fire · his teacher again
timeline/stages/1/summary: Dante joined the guild of doctors and apothecaries and stepped into politics. He became a prior — and with his own hand banished his closest friend.
timeline/stages/1/events/0/summary: Under the Ordinances of Justice, the poet joins the guild of doctors and apothecaries to win the right to take part in government. Under the surface, the Whites and the Blacks are already stirring.
timeline/stages/1/events/1/summary: Rome in its Jubilee year, Florence with Dante as prior; on the banishment list is his best friend's name. The Divine Comedy is set in this year.
timeline/stages/1/events/1/comedyAnchor/: Old Cavalcanti: where is my son?
timeline/stages/2/summary: Tried in his absence, banished for life, sentenced to burn. Under other men's roofs, Dante began to write the Divine Comedy.
timeline/stages/2/events/0/summary: The pope holds the envoy, the Blacks seize the city, the trial goes on without him: a fine, exile, and burning if he will not confess. He never set foot in Florence again.
timeline/stages/2/events/0/comedyAnchor/: Another man's bread · the pope planted upside down
timeline/stages/2/events/1/summary: The shame of eating at a great lord's table, the break with the exiled Whites; the choice to write in the everyday tongue, and the words over the gate of Hell.
timeline/stages/2/events/1/comedyAnchor/: The words over the gate of Hell
timeline/stages/2/events/2/summary: Henry VII comes south, and Dante writes open letter after open letter, staking everything. In 1313, at Buonconvento, the emperor falls suddenly ill and dies. The dream breaks.
timeline/stages/2/events/2/comedyAnchor/: The empty seat kept for Henry
timeline/stages/2/events/3/summary: Pay the fine, put on the penitent's robe, walk through the streets to the Baptistery — and he could go home. He refused: “Home by that road? Never.”
timeline/stages/2/events/3/comedyAnchor/: If ever this sacred poem brings me home
timeline/stages/3/summary: Guido Novello's welcome, his children around him again, the Paradiso finished. In September 1321 the poet was laid to rest in Ravenna.
timeline/stages/3/events/0/summary: Pine woods and golden mosaics, the test by three apostles, the fever caught on the way back from Venice, and the tale of the thirteen lost cantos.
events/1265_firenze/phases/0/narrative: 1373 年，佛罗伦萨，圣斯特凡诺教堂。史上第一个「但丁讲席」开讲——主讲人：乔万尼·薄伽丘。
events/1265_firenze/phases/0/instruction: 点击讲坛上的薄伽丘，听他开讲。
events/1265_firenze/phases/0/npcs/0/dial: 1265 年，双子座下，这座城里生下一个婴儿。
五十年后，同一座城判他火刑。
今天，城里付钱请我来讲他。诸位——我们从头讲。
events/1265_firenze/phases/1/narrative: 1265 年 5 月，佛罗伦萨。阿利吉耶里家添丁，取名杜兰特，小名——但丁。
events/1265_firenze/phases/1/instruction: 在洗礼堂前的市集走动，听听这座城的人都在说什么。
events/1265_firenze/phases/1/npcs/0/dial: 行会的旗子比领主的剑管用，这就是佛罗伦萨。
呢绒、钱庄、香料——我们靠生意吃饭，不靠城堡。
events/1265_firenze/phases/1/npcs/1/dial: 五年前，蒙塔佩尔蒂。吉伯林党借西耶纳的兵杀回来……
阿尔比亚河的水，都染红了。
皇帝党、教皇党——这座城的孩子生下来，就得选一边。
events/1265_firenze/phases/1/npcs/2/dial: 阿利吉耶里家？小贵族，贵尔夫党的——就是教皇党。
听说孩子他母亲有孕时，梦见自己在月桂树下产子呢。
events/1265_firenze/phases/1/npcs/3/dial: 看见那座八角的洗礼堂了吗？圣乔万尼——我们「美丽的圣约翰」。
洗礼堂的圣水池——这城里每一个孩子，都从这里开始。
events/1265_firenze/phases/1/npcs/4/dial: 八角形的洗礼堂立在广场中央，大理石的墙面在晨光里发亮。来年开春的圣周六，那个叫但丁的婴儿将随全城的新生儿一起，在这里受洗。
events/1265_firenze/phases/2/prompt: 高祖讲的是他自己的一生。按先后排回去。
events/1265_firenze/phases/2/revealNote:
一座城、一个家、一场婚姻、一次远征——最后落在一个婴儿身上。
他讲的不是历史，是在讲这个孩子从哪里来。
events/1265_firenze/phases/3/narrative: 讲坛上，薄伽丘翻开《天堂》第十五歌——但丁的高祖、十字军烈士卡恰圭达，追忆古老纯朴的佛罗伦萨。
events/1265_firenze/phases/3/instruction: 点击画面，一格一格看下去。
events/1265_firenze/phases/3/panels/0/di: 「佛罗伦萨，在古老的城墙之内，安于朴素与贞静。钟声报着晨祷与午祷，一如往昔。」
events/1265_firenze/phases/3/panels/1/di: 「主妇守着纺锤和纱线，在摇篮边用古老的故事，讲特洛伊、菲埃索莱和罗马。」
events/1265_firenze/phases/3/panels/2/di: 「我的妻子从波河谷来，你们的姓氏——阿利吉耶里——就是从她而来。」
events/1265_firenze/phases/3/panels/3/di: 「后来我随皇帝康拉德东征，在圣地为信仰而死，从殉道来到这平安之境。」
events/1265_firenze/phases/3/panels/4/di: 来年开春的圣周六。婴儿在圣乔万尼洗礼堂受洗，取名杜兰特·阿利吉耶里。
「我的血脉里，将出一个走遍三界的人。」
events/1265_firenze/phases/4/narrative: 九年过去。阿利吉耶里家的少年在羊皮纸和抄本之间长大。母亲早逝，父亲做着放贷的小生意。
events/1265_firenze/phases/4/instruction: 点击书房里的物件与家人。
events/1265_firenze/phases/4/npcs/0/dial: 案上摊着一部《埃涅阿斯纪》抄本——曼图亚人维吉尔的史诗。书页边写满了稚拙的批注。
这位曼图亚人……我的老师。
events/1265_firenze/phases/4/npcs/1/dial: 角落里放着一支落了灰的纺锤。母亲贝拉在他年幼时便去世了。
……月桂树下的梦，是真的吗，母亲？
events/1265_firenze/phases/4/npcs/2/dial: 又在看书？也好。我们这样的小门户，笔比剑稳妥。
明日贵人家有宴席，你随我去。穿体面些。
events/1265_firenze/phases/5/transitionT:
九岁那年五月，他在宴席上看见一个穿绯红衣裙的女孩。
他后来写道：
「看哪，一个比我更强的神，来主宰我了。」
events/1265_firenze/phases/5/announcemen: 薄伽丘：「诸位，请记住那件绯红的衣裙。一个九岁孩子的心动，将变成基督教世界最庞大的一首诗。」
quiz/1265_firenze/quizzes/0/question: 但丁出生的佛罗伦萨，当时最深的政治裂痕是哪两党之争？
quiz/1265_firenze/quizzes/0/options/1: 贵尔夫党（教皇党）与吉伯林党（皇帝党）
quiz/1265_firenze/quizzes/0/explanation: 13 世纪的意大利分裂为拥护教皇的贵尔夫党与拥护神圣罗马皇帝的吉伯林党。1260 年蒙塔佩尔蒂之战中，吉伯林党借西耶纳军队大败佛罗伦萨的贵尔夫党。白党与黑党是后来贵尔夫党内部的分裂。
quiz/1265_firenze/quizzes/1/question: 《天堂》第十五歌里，向但丁追忆「古老纯朴的佛罗伦萨」的先祖是谁？
quiz/1265_firenze/quizzes/1/explanation: 卡恰圭达是但丁的高祖，随皇帝康拉德三世参加第二次十字军东征战死。《天堂》XV–XVII 中他追忆旧城、预言但丁的流亡。阿利吉耶里的姓氏即来自他的妻子。
quiz/1265_firenze/quizzes/2/question:
九岁的但丁初见贝雅特丽切后写道：
「看哪，一个比我更___的神，来主宰我了」
quiz/1265_firenze/quizzes/2/explanation: 出自《新生》第二章。九岁的但丁在宴席上初见贝雅特丽切，自此「爱神主宰了我的灵魂」——这次心动最终长成了《神曲》。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/0/transition: 讲坛上，薄伽丘翻开《新生》。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/0/announceme: 薄伽丘：「他一生只与她说过几次话。她嫁了银行家，他娶了政治联姻的妻子。可《神曲》里引他上天堂的不是妻子——是她。何以至此？」
events/1283_beatrice/phases/1/narrative: 十八岁。晨光里的阿诺河。一位白衣的女子与两名女伴从桥上走来。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/1/instructio: 点击桥头的人，把这一刻记下来。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/1/npcs/0/dia: 她走过桥头，转过脸来，向他微微颔首致意。
那一刻，我仿佛看到了幸福的极限。
她的致意里有一种无法言说的谦和。我如痴如醉，像逃离人群的人一样跑回房间，开始想她。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/1/npcs/1/dia: 又失魂落魄了？把它写下来，杜兰特。
我们写的是「温柔新体」——爱不是骑士的战利品，是让灵魂高贵起来的东西。
写好了拿来给我看。你叫我第一好友，可不能拿平庸的十四行糊弄我。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/1/npcs/2/dia: 那位是波尔蒂纳里家的碧丝——已许给巴尔迪家的人了。
满城的诗人都在写她。她只是照旧向每个人温和地问好。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/2/transition:
1289 年六月，坎帕尔迪诺。二十四岁的但丁在前排轻骑兵里，打了一整天。
他后来几乎从不提这场仗。

战争结束了。
但第二年夏天，佛罗伦萨的丧钟，
为一个二十四岁的女人而鸣。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/3/panels/0/d: 桥头空了。再没有那声温和的致意。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/3/panels/1/d: 白衣的送葬队列捧着白花，穿过全城。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/3/panels/2/d: 他在《新生》里引《耶利米哀歌》哭她——像哭一座陷落的圣城。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/4/narrative: 悲痛之后，《新生》要有一个结尾。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/4/question: 悲痛之后，你要为她写什么？
events/1283_beatrice/phases/4/options/1/: 此后不再写她——直到能「以前人未有的方式写她」

在配得上她之前，我搁笔。
若上天假我以年，我要为她写下前人未曾为任何女子写过的东西。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/4/conclusion: 《新生》就此收束。他真的停笔了。这个誓言要等二十年、等他失去一切之后，才以一万四千余行的规模兑现——誓言的兑现，从她在炼狱山顶等他开始：「看着我，我正是，正是贝雅特丽切。」
events/1283_beatrice/phases/5/transition: 讲坛上，薄伽丘把《新生》的终章与《炼狱》第三十歌并排摊开。
events/1283_beatrice/phases/5/announceme: 薄伽丘：「诸位——她不是他的『女友』。她是他给自己造的神。懂了这一点，才算摸到《神曲》的门。」
quiz/1283_beatrice/quizzes/0/question: 1289 年，但丁作为轻骑兵参加了哪场战役？
quiz/1283_beatrice/quizzes/0/explanation: 1289 年佛罗伦萨与阿雷佐会战于坎帕尔迪诺平原，但丁在前排轻骑兵中亲历此战，自述「恐惧极大，最后又变成极大的喜悦」。蒙塔佩尔蒂（1260）在他出生前，拉斯特拉（1304）是流亡白党的惨败。
quiz/1283_beatrice/quizzes/1/question: 贝雅特丽切死后，但丁在《新生》结尾立下了什么誓言？
quiz/1283_beatrice/quizzes/1/options/0: 为她写尽哀歌，然后放下
quiz/1283_beatrice/quizzes/1/options/2: 此后不再写她，直到能以前人未有的方式写她
quiz/1283_beatrice/quizzes/1/explanation: 《新生》终章：但丁决定搁笔，直到能「为她写下前人未曾为任何女子写过的东西」。二十年后，这个誓言以《神曲》兑现——她成为引他上天堂的向导。
quiz/1283_beatrice/quizzes/2/question:
《炼狱》第三十歌，她在炼狱山顶现身时说：
「看着我，我正是，正是___」
quiz/1283_beatrice/quizzes/2/explanation: 《炼狱》XXX：维吉尔悄然退场，贝雅特丽切登场——「Guardaci ben! Ben son, ben son Beatrice.」桥头一别，再见已在炼狱山顶，《新生》的誓言在此兑现。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/0/transition: 薄伽丘翻过一页，停住了。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/0/announceme:
我们其实不知道但丁是怎么认识布鲁内托·拉蒂尼的。没有学籍，没有契约，没有一封信。
我们知道有这么一位老师，只有一个原因——但丁在《地狱》里写了他。
记住这件事：现实这一半的证据，来自文学那一半。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/0/dufu_react:
所以今天这一课，要倒着上。
先看他们在人世间怎么相处——再看学生把老师写去了哪里。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/1/title: 佛罗伦萨 · 老师的书房 · 1292
events/1292_brunetto/phases/1/narrative: 贝雅特丽切死后两年。二十七岁的但丁把自己埋进书里。城里最有学问的老人是布鲁内托·拉蒂尼——公证人、前公社书记长、教这座城怎么说话、怎么议政的人。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/1/instructio: 跟老师聊聊。留意他桌上那两本书。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/1/npcs/0/dia: 会写诗不算本事，孩子。这城里会写诗的人，比会读的还多。
本事是：让一座城听懂你。修辞学不是装饰，是政治。你要从政，先学会怎么把话说进别人心里。

人这一辈子很短。但人能让自己不朽——靠留下一样比自己活得久的东西。
你现在还不懂我在说什么。以后会懂。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/1/npcs/1/dia: 老师毕生的大书：一部把全世界的学问收进来的百科。天文、历史、伦理、修辞、如何治理一座城——什么都有。
蒙塔佩尔蒂之后我流亡法国，那六年写的。法语通行得远，读的人多。学问要传得出去才叫学问。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/1/npcs/2/dia: 旁边一本薄的，意大利俗语写的韵文。诗里，作者在一座树林中迷了路，遇见一位女神，被带着游历万物之理。
……在树林里迷路。被一个人领着走。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/1/npcs/3/dia: 先生年纪大了。你来得算晚的——他从法国回来快三十年了。
全城的人都受过他的教。人家说，是他把佛罗伦萨人「教粗为细」的。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/2/narrative: 老师的大书用法文写，小书用俗语写。有一天但丁也要选。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/2/question: 如果要写一本能活得比自己久的书，该用哪种语言？
events/1292_brunetto/phases/2/options/0/: 拉丁文——学者的语言，最体面
体面。可你母亲读不了，你邻居读不了。你要写给谁看？
events/1292_brunetto/phases/2/options/1/: 法文——像老师那样，传得远

我就是这么选的。读的人确实多。
……只是，那不是我出生时说的话。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/2/options/2/: 俗语——我在佛罗伦萨街上学会的那种话

如果一样东西要活得比我久，它得用活着的语言写。
拉丁文是死的，法文不是我的。
我要用我母亲教我的那种话，写一本谁都能读的书。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/2/conclusion:
这个选择在 1292 年还只是一句空话。十几年后，一个流亡在外、身无分文的人，会用它写出一部三行连锁韵的长诗——用「俗语」，而不是任何一种体面的语言。那部诗后来把这种「俗语」变成了意大利语。
而他的老师，选了另一条路。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/3/token/deta: 1292 · 布鲁内托·拉蒂尼，教他修辞、政治，与「如何使人不朽」
events/1292_brunetto/phases/3/prompt: 把「老师」放进但丁的手稿
events/1292_brunetto/phases/3/afterTitle: 三十年后 · 地狱 第十五歌
events/1292_brunetto/phases/3/afterText:
第七圈，第三环。
火雨落在沙上，一落就是永远。
一群亡魂沿着堤岸走过来，眯着眼打量他。
其中一个，忽然抓住了他的衣角。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/4/soul/metLa: 1292 佛罗伦萨 · 老师的书房
events/1292_brunetto/phases/4/recognitio:
那张脸被火燎得看不清了。
但丁俯下身，盯了很久，才认出来——

「您在这儿吗，布鲁内托先生？」
events/1292_brunetto/phases/4/asks/0/q: 你敬重他。他为什么在这里？
events/1292_brunetto/phases/4/asks/0/a:
因为敬重不替他免罪。
我把他判进「违逆自然」这一环。这是全书最难写的一段。
如果我因为爱一个人，就把他挪到他不该在的地方——
那这整座地狱，一文不值。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/4/asks/1/q: 那你为什么还用敬称叫他「您」？
events/1292_brunetto/phases/4/asks/1/a:
整本书里我用「您」的人，五个都不到。
判他的是我，敬他的也是我。这两件事我不打算调和。
你刚才听见那句「您教我如何使人不朽」——
那不是客套。那是我欠他的。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/4/asks/2/a:
他没有替自己辩解一个字。
他只托付了一样东西：他的《宝库》。
「让我的《宝库》托付给你——我在那本书里还活着。」
然后他就跑开了。像维罗纳赛跑抢那块绿布的人——
看上去还是赢的那一个，不是输的那一个。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/4/asks/3/q: 把他写进这里，是惩罚他，还是救他？
events/1292_brunetto/phases/4/asks/3/a:
你自己想。
七百年过去了。人们记得布鲁内托·拉蒂尼，
不是因为那部法文的《宝库》——
是因为我把他放在了火雨底下。
他要的那个「不朽」，我给他了。用的是这个方式。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/4/closing:
他教但丁：人如何让自己不朽。
但丁做到了——然后把老师一起带了进去。

现实里的一位老师，成了《地狱》第十五歌里的一个亡魂。
《神曲》就是这么盖起来的：他把自己认识的人，一个一个放了进去。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/5/speaker: 布鲁内托 · 《地狱》第十五歌
events/1292_brunetto/phases/5/quote:
「你若跟着你的星走，必定能抵达光荣的港口……
可那一群忘恩负义的恶毒之民，将要因为你做的好事与你为敌。
躲开他们。」
events/1292_brunetto/phases/5/instructio: 先别急着往下读。把这三块时间，各归各位。

（故事里的时间）

events/1292_brunetto/phases/5/axis/2/lab:

缺席审判，终身放逐
events/1292_brunetto/phases/5/blocks/2/t:
约 1310 年代
流亡途中，寄人篱下
events/1292_brunetto/phases/5/question: 那这到底是预言，还是回忆？
events/1292_brunetto/phases/5/conclusion:
布鲁内托以为自己在说未来。
但丁写这段的时候，那个「未来」已经过去十几年了。

他让书里的人「预言」他早就吃过的苦。
所以《神曲》里每一次预言，都是双份的：
人物在往前看，作者在往回看，两道目光在 1300 年这一点上对撞。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/6/transition: 讲坛上，薄伽丘合上第十五歌。
events/1292_brunetto/phases/6/dufu_react:
六百年来，学者们为一件事吵个不停：
布鲁内托到底犯了什么「违逆自然」的罪？
有人说是肉身的罪。也有人说——
他背弃了自己的母语，用法文写了毕生的大书。

哪一种说法对，我们不知道。
但你注意到没有：判他的那个人，正是那个决定用母语写作的人。
quiz/1292_brunetto/quizzes/0/question: 布鲁内托·拉蒂尼毕生的大书《宝库》，是用什么语言写的？
quiz/1292_brunetto/quizzes/0/explanation: 蒙塔佩尔蒂战败后布鲁内托流亡法国，在那里用法文写下百科式的《宝库》——他的理由是法语通行得远。他另有一部意大利俗语的韵文《小宝库》，但分量小得多。这个选择，后来成了理解《地狱》第十五歌的关键之一。
quiz/1292_brunetto/quizzes/1/question: 但丁在《地狱》里重遇布鲁内托时，做了一件全书只对极少数人做的事。是什么？
quiz/1292_brunetto/quizzes/1/explanation: 全诗中但丁用敬称 voi（您）的亡魂不超过五个。他把老师判进了地狱，却仍然用敬语跟他说话——判决与敬意同时成立，这正是这一歌最难的地方。
quiz/1292_brunetto/quizzes/2/question:
《地狱》第十五歌，但丁对老师说的那句话：
「您教过我，人如何使自己___」
quiz/1292_brunetto/quizzes/2/explanation: 「m'insegnavate come l'uom s'etterna」——您教我，人如何使自己不朽。布鲁内托教会了他这件事；而但丁让老师不朽的方式，是把他写进了火雨底下的第七圈。
events/1295_arte/phases/0/transitionText: 讲坛上，薄伽丘合上《新生》，换了一册城邦档案。
events/1295_arte/phases/0/announcement/t: 薄伽丘：「要害死一个诗人，先让他从政。1295 年，他去登记了行会——医生和药剂师的行会。别笑：书在当时，按药材归类。」
events/1295_arte/phases/1/narrative: 《正义法规》颁布：豪族不得任公职，参政须注册行会。三十岁的但丁走进药柜与天平之间，来办一件改变命运的手续。
events/1295_arte/phases/1/instruction: 在行会大厅里办登记，顺便听听佛罗伦萨的新党争。
events/1295_arte/phases/1/npcs/0/dialogu: 姓名？杜兰特·阿利吉耶里。职业？……诗人。
新颁的《正义法规》您知道吧？针对的就是那些跋扈的豪族——平民做官，须入行会。
登记医生与药剂师行会，年费缴讫。恭喜，您现在有参政资格了。
events/1295_arte/phases/1/npcs/1/dialogu: 别皱眉——香料、药材、颜料、书籍，都是稀罕的舶来品，同一条商路运来的。
events/1295_arte/phases/1/npcs/2/dialogu: 维吉尔的新抄本，波隆那来的，要吗？给您算便宜。
如今识字的人多了，佛罗伦萨的算学学校比修道院还热闹。书，是门好生意。
events/1295_arte/phases/1/npcs/3/dialogu: 多纳蒂家的科尔索大人，今早又在广场骂人了——他们那伙人如今叫「黑党」。
切尔基家做买卖发的家，有钱，新贵，一伙人称「白党」。同是贵尔夫党，狗咬狗。
吉伯林党——拥皇帝的那一派？早赶出城啦。如今满城都是拥教皇的贵尔夫党。没了外敌，自家人斗自家人。
events/1295_arte/phases/2/narrative: 手续办完。暮色里的老桥上，同侪们等着他。
events/1295_arte/phases/2/instruction: 和桥上的朋友说说话，再听听自己的心。
events/1295_arte/phases/2/npcs/0/dialogu: 政治是烂泥，杜兰特。你我是写诗的。
（说这话的圭多，自己正是白党的大人物。）
events/1295_arte/phases/2/npcs/1/dialogu: 哟，「阁下」！医药行会的大人物！以后抓药找你打折吗？
回头再跟你对骂几首十四行——上回你损我的那首，我还没还嘴呢。
（福雷塞是科尔索的弟弟，也是但丁的酒友。两人互写打油诗互损，字字见血，情谊也是真的。）
events/1295_arte/phases/2/npcs/2/dialogu: 圭多说政治是烂泥。可是——
城应当像诗一样有秩序。我要去给它写秩序。
events/1295_arte/phases/3/lede:
你是佛罗伦萨一家的当家人。对面那一家和你不是一党。
每一次城里换了人说了算，当权的那一方要决定：把对面赶出去，还是让他们留下。
被赶走的人不会消失——他们会在别的城里等，等着带外援回来。
events/1295_arte/phases/3/coda/lines/0: 1300 年，但丁在放逐名单上签了字。名单上有他最好的朋友。
events/1295_arte/phases/3/coda/lines/1: 他签的时候相信：规矩对两党一样，城就能安定下来。
events/1295_arte/phases/3/coda/lines/2: 1302 年，同一套规矩把他自己赶了出去。
events/1295_arte/phases/3/coda/lines/3: 1315 年，佛罗伦萨说：缴罚金、穿悔罪服、游街到洗礼堂，就让你回来。他拒绝了。
events/1295_arte/phases/3/coda/lines/4: 佛罗伦萨的毛病从来不是谁比谁坏。是这座城把「放逐」变成了一手可以反复再打的棋——
events/1295_arte/phases/3/coda/lines/5: 输的人总能带外援回来，赢的人知道这一点，所以下手一次比一次狠。
events/1295_arte/phases/3/coda/turn:
然后他写了《地狱》。
那是一个只有一轮的世界：判决下了就不再改，没有下一次交手，没有回来的路。

而地狱最底下的一层，不是杀人，不是暴力——
是背叛。是把信任毁掉的人。
那一层是冻住的：在那里，什么都不会再变了。
events/1295_arte/phases/4/transitionText: 讲坛上换了一个声音——彼得罗·阿利吉耶里，但丁之子，《神曲》最早的注疏人之一。
events/1295_arte/phases/4/announcement/t: 后世回声 · 彼得罗注疏
「父亲相信城邦可以被理性治理。后来在《地狱》第六歌，他让暴食者恰科预言这座城的撕裂——两党相争，血流成河。那预言，其实是回忆。他还借恰科之口点破病根：傲慢、嫉妒和贪婪，是燃烧人心的三粒火星。」
quiz/1295_arte/quizzes/0/question: 1295 年，但丁为了取得参政资格注册了哪个行会？
quiz/1295_arte/quizzes/0/explanation: 按《正义法规》，参政须入行会。书籍当时按药材归类、书商挂靠医药行会——于是诗人注册了医生与药剂师行会。
quiz/1295_arte/quizzes/1/question: 1290 年代佛罗伦萨贵尔夫党分裂出的「白党」与「黑党」，领袖家族分别是？

quiz/1295_arte/quizzes/1/options/3: 斯卡拉家（白）/ 维斯孔蒂家（黑）
quiz/1295_arte/quizzes/1/explanation: 白党以经商暴富的新贵切尔基家为首，黑党以老贵族多纳蒂家的科尔索为首。同属贵尔夫党，却斗得你死我活——但丁一家属白党。

《地狱》第六歌，恰科预言佛罗伦萨的撕裂：

events/1300_priore/phases/0/transitionTe: 讲坛上，薄伽丘写下一个年份：1300。
events/1300_priore/phases/0/announcement: 薄伽丘：「记住这一年。史实里，他在这一年当上执政官；而《神曲》的故事，也被他放在这一年——人生的中点。为什么？听完你们就懂了。」
events/1300_priore/phases/1/travelNarrat: 教皇卜尼法斯八世首创「禧年」：凡今年至罗马朝圣者，罪愆全赦。二十万人涌向罗马——但丁也在其中。
events/1300_priore/phases/1/waypoints/0/: 满城的人都在收拾行装。去罗马！去禧年！
events/1300_priore/phases/1/waypoints/1/: 古道上人流不断：香客、商贩、乞丐、贵妇的轿子。所有语言都在说同一个词——罗马。
events/1300_priore/phases/1/waypoints/2/: 城门内外，人流如蚁。桥上的人群被分成两列对向而行，才不至于踩踏。
像军队渡桥，分两列……这个画面，我记下了。
events/1300_priore/phases/2/narrative: 罗马。二十万朝圣者把街道挤成河流。
events/1300_priore/phases/2/npcs/0/dialo: 维持秩序的兵丁把桥面从中隔开：去圣彼得堂的靠一边，回程的靠另一边。
多年以后，我写地狱第八层的恶囊：罪人分两列对向而行——「就像禧年时罗马桥上的人流」。
events/1300_priore/phases/2/npcs/1/dialo: 各地口音的圣歌混在一处。有人一路膝行，膝盖磨出了血。

events/1302_esilio/phases/1/title: Rome · The pope's audience hall · Autumn 1301
events/1302_esilio/phases/1/narrative: The Blacks want the French king's brother, Charles of Valois, to come and “make peace” in Florence. The city sends three envoys to Rome to put its case to the pope — Dante is one of them.
events/1302_esilio/phases/1/instruction: Listen carefully in the hall: who is kept, and who is sent away.
events/1302_esilio/phases/1/npcs/0/dialo: Children of Florence, why so anxious? We ask only that your city obey.
The other envoys may go home and carry Our word. This poet — he stays here with Us.
events/1302_esilio/phases/1/npcs/1/dialo: (quietly) Lord Charles of Valois has already marched north with his troops, to “make peace” in Florence.
The Holy Father says: what's your hurry? Stay a few more days.
events/1302_esilio/phases/1/npcs/2/dialo: Make peace? You don't bring a single soldier to make peace.
Keeping me here in Rome… something is about to happen in the city.
events/1302_esilio/phases/2/situation:
The pope sends the other two envoys back to Florence and keeps you alone.
At the same moment, the French king's brother Charles of Valois is marching north with an army — officially, to “make peace.”
events/1302_esilio/phases/2/options/0/te: Charles really does make peace, and both parties give ground
events/1302_esilio/phases/2/options/1/te: The Blacks open the gates to him and the Whites are crushed
events/1302_esilio/phases/2/options/2/te: The Whites hold the city and Charles goes home with nothing
events/1302_esilio/phases/2/sameNote: You guessed it. So you already know what this “peace” was — now watch it land on you.
events/1302_esilio/phases/2/diffNote: It went the other way. Watch how it happened —
events/1302_esilio/phases/2/consequence:
The Blacks opened the gates for Charles. Corso Donati came back. They burned the Whites' houses and looted the Whites' shops, for six days.
Only then came the trials.
events/1302_esilio/phases/3/title: The road home · Bad news all the way
events/1302_esilio/phases/3/travelNarrat: At last the pope lets him go. On the road home, the news is worse at every stop.
events/1302_esilio/phases/3/instruction: Click each stop along the road.
events/1302_esilio/phases/3/waypoints/0/: “Charles is in the city! He didn't lose a single soldier — the gates opened by themselves.”
events/1302_esilio/phases/3/waypoints/1/: “The Blacks opened the gates for Charles, and Corso Donati is back in the city. They're burning the Whites' houses and looting the Whites' shops.”
events/1302_esilio/phases/3/waypoints/2/: “The new government is trying the Whites without them there… Signor Alighieri — you're on the list.”
events/1302_esilio/phases/4/title: Inn outside the walls · Working it out on a snowy night
events/1302_esilio/phases/4/narrative: An inn outside Florence. Snow at night. A copy of the sentence is being passed around among the White refugees. What actually happened — put the clues together.
events/1302_esilio/phases/4/instruction: Collect all 5 clues and work out what this trial really was.
events/1302_esilio/phases/4/npcs/0/dialo: “Dante Alighieri: taking bribes, extorting money he had no right to, opposing the pope and Lord Charles — a fine of five thousand florins, two years' exile, and never to hold public office again.”
Bribes? Every account I kept as prior would stand up to inspection. The charge is made up.
events/1302_esilio/phases/4/npcs/1/dialo: Confess and pay by the deadline and they cut the sentence — but confessing means admitting that the Blacks' government is the lawful one.
Confess, and you convict yourself. Refuse, and they get to take your life. Both ways are dead ends.
events/1302_esilio/phases/4/npcs/2/dialo: “The men named above have refused to appear — if any of them falls into the hands of the commune, let him be burned with fire until he dies. (igne comburatur sic quod moriatur)”
The stake. They mean to burn me alive.
events/1302_esilio/phases/4/npcs/3/dialo: Your lady asked me to bring word: “Gemma is staying in the city with the children. She is a Donati daughter — the Blacks will not touch her.”
“Don't come back.” — that was all your lady said.
events/1302_esilio/phases/4/npcs/4/dialo: Fifteen men were sentenced to burn with him on 10 March. Then look at the sentence lists, batch after batch — everyone on them is a leading White. Without exception.
events/1302_esilio/phases/5/narrative: The fire is dying down. Put all the clues together — what was this trial really?
events/1302_esilio/phases/5/options/0/te: I was unlucky. I got caught in a coup.
events/1302_esilio/phases/5/options/0/re: …No. Look again: the timing, the charges, the list. Who is behind all of it?
events/1302_esilio/phases/5/options/1/te: The pope used Charles's sword to purge the Whites — I'm an enemy removed “by law”
events/1302_esilio/phases/5/options/1/re:
Boniface held me in Rome so that Charles's sword could walk in unopposed.
The Blacks held the knife, the French cleared the road, the pope moved the pieces.
The charges were fake, the trial was real — because the trial itself was the weapon.
events/1302_esilio/phases/5/conclusion/n: The charges, the timing, the list — settle on the conclusion first. Next step: prove it.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/claim: This trial was not justice. It was a political purge that used the law as a weapon.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/instruction: Out of what you saw at the inn, pick the 2 things that really support this claim.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/items/0/text: The sentence charges him with “taking bribes and extorting money he had no right to” — but Dante was a prior for two months in all.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/items/0/why: The charge doesn't match the facts, and from first to last not one account book was ever produced. The charge was fitted on afterwards — which means convicting him was never the point.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/items/1/text: The fifteen men sentenced to burn with him on 10 March were all leading Whites, without exception.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/items/1/why: If they were really investigating bribery, the list of the accused would not line up exactly with one party. A list that tidy means people were picked by party, not by crime.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/items/2/text: The second sentence raised the punishment from fine and exile to burning.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/items/2/why: Harsh is not the same as political. A real thief who refuses to appear could have his sentence raised too. This shows they were in a hurry, but on its own it doesn't get you to “purge.”
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/items/3/text: It was snowing in Florence the days the sentence was read out.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/items/3/why: True, but it has nothing to do with the claim. Evidence has to hold the conclusion up. Being true is not enough.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/items/4/text: Gemma stayed in the city with the children and was never touched — she is a Donati daughter.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/items/4/why: This one actually pulls the other way: the Blacks kept family ties, they did not kill every White they saw. True, and important — but it does not support “the trial was a weapon.” Good reasoning means recognising which facts work against you.
events/1302_esilio/phases/6/closing:
Two are enough: the charge, and the list.
The charge doesn't fit, and yet the list covers one party exactly — so what they were handling was not a court case.
events/1302_esilio/phases/7/token/detail: 1302 · Tried in absence, exiled for life, burned if he will not appear
events/1302_esilio/phases/7/afterText:
He has an ancestor, speaking in 1300, “foretell” what had already happened in 1302:

“You shall leave behind everything you love most — that is the first arrow the bow of exile shoots.
You shall taste how salty another man's bread is, and how steep another man's stairs are.”

In that same book, he also gave everyone a new place.
events/1302_esilio/phases/8/question: These people — which realm did Dante put each of them in?
events/1302_esilio/phases/8/circles/1/la: Sins that can still be washed clean
events/1302_esilio/phases/8/circles/2/la: Sins that can never be washed clean
events/1302_esilio/phases/8/souls/0/verd: Inferno XIX: in the third ditch of the eighth circle, the men who bought and sold holy office are stuffed head-down into cracks in the rock, with only the soles of their feet left outside to burn. Dante comes to the edge of one hole. Down inside it, Nicholas III mistakes him for someone else and “foretells” that the next man to fill this hole will be Boniface. — When Dante wrote this, Boniface was still alive. He put a living man into Hell, and kept the place ready for him in advance.
events/1302_esilio/phases/8/souls/0/hint: His sin has to do with “money” and “holy office.”
events/1302_esilio/phases/8/souls/1/verd: Head of the Blacks, the man who drove Dante out of the city. Dante does not sentence him with his own hand — he has Corso's own younger brother Forese say it, up in Purgatory: “The one most to blame will be dragged along by a beast, faster and faster, all the way down to the valley where the sin is never washed clean.” (Purgatorio XXIV) Two brothers: one in Purgatory, one below.
events/1302_esilio/phases/8/souls/2/verd: Purgatorio XXIII: the gluttons are so starved that they have lost their shape, and Dante almost fails to recognise his old friend. When they were young the two of them wrote poems insulting each other — really nasty ones. Yet meeting again in Purgatory, they fall into talk as if none of it had happened. — Not everyone he loved is up above, and not everyone who did wrong is down below.
events/1302_esilio/phases/8/souls/2/hint: He is Corso's brother, but he is not Corso.
events/1302_esilio/phases/8/souls/3/metL: 1283 Florence · by the Santa Trinita bridge
events/1302_esilio/phases/8/souls/3/verd: She appears in Purgatorio XXX, takes Dante over from Virgil, and leads him all the way to the final light of Paradiso XXXIII. The girl in the crimson dress at that party, when he was nine years old, ends up as the guide for the whole poem.
events/1302_esilio/phases/8/souls/3/hint: She is the one who leads the way.
events/1302_esilio/phases/9/transitionTe: Boccaccio puts down his lecture notes.
events/1302_esilio/phases/9/dufu_reactio:
The man you just put into Hell was talking to you in Rome a quarter of an hour ago.

That is how this book was made. He did not invent a Hell —
he took Florence, and Rome, and everyone he knew in his life,
and seated them all over again, level by level.
quiz/1302_esilio/quizzes/0/question: What was Dante charged with at the 1302 trial held without him?
quiz/1302_esilio/quizzes/0/options/1: Taking bribes (the charge was made up)
quiz/1302_esilio/quizzes/0/options/3: Refusing to serve as a soldier
quiz/1302_esilio/quizzes/0/explanation: The sentence of 27 January 1302 fined him and sent him into exile for “taking bribes and extorting money he had no right to” — and no evidence was ever produced. It was a political purge: Pope Boniface VIII used Charles of Valois's sword, and the Blacks carried it out.
quiz/1302_esilio/quizzes/1/question: The second sentence, on 10 March 1302, said that if Florence caught Dante he would be punished how?
quiz/1302_esilio/quizzes/1/explanation: The second sentence says it in so many words: “if he falls into the hands of the commune, let him be burned with fire until he dies” (igne comburatur sic quod moriatur). Beheading was the changed sentence, after he refused the amnesty in 1315.
quiz/1302_esilio/quizzes/2/question:
Paradiso XVII: his ancestor Cacciaguida foretells the exile.
“You shall taste how ___ another man's bread is, and how steep another man's stairs are”
quiz/1302_esilio/quizzes/2/explanation: The exile prophecy in Paradiso XVII is one of the most famous passages in the Divine Comedy — “come sa di sale lo pane altrui.” The writing turns time around: Dante, already in exile, has his ancestor “foretell” to his 1300 self everything that has already happened.
events/1308_inferno/phases/0/transitionT: 讲坛上，薄伽丘念《飨宴》里的一句自述。
events/1308_inferno/phases/0/announcemen: 「我是一条无帆无舵的船，被干燥的贫穷之风，吹往各处的港口、河口与海岸。」——薄伽丘：「流亡第六年。接下来诸位要看的，是一个人沉到底，然后在底上动笔。」
events/1308_inferno/phases/1/title: 维罗纳 · 斯卡拉宫廊下
events/1308_inferno/phases/1/narrative: 寄人篱下的日子。维罗纳，斯卡拉家的宫廷——恩主的面包，末席的座位。
events/1308_inferno/phases/1/instruction: 在廊下走一走，看看寄食者的处境。
events/1308_inferno/phases/1/npcs/0/dial: 阿利吉耶里先生，今晚宴席您坐末席——靠门那头。
别见怪，座次按身份排。您如今……嗯。
events/1308_inferno/phases/1/npcs/1/dial: 宫里人人有用处：我逗大人笑，厨子喂饱大人，兵护着大人。
诗人？哈！诗人是饭后的果盘——有你不多，没你不少。
events/1308_inferno/phases/1/npcs/2/dial: 阿利吉耶里！弟兄们在集结，联合吉伯林党，武力打回佛罗伦萨！
你的名字还在我们的名册上。你不来——就是叛徒。
events/1308_inferno/phases/1/npcs/3/dial: 先生，别理他们。给我讲讲维吉尔吧——昨天讲到第六卷，埃涅阿斯下到冥界……
（斯卡拉家的小公子，全宫廷唯一拿他当老师敬的人。多年后，《天堂》将题献给成年的坎格兰德。）
events/1308_inferno/phases/2/narrative: 白党使者站在廊下等答复。武力还乡——回家的路，还是死路？
events/1308_inferno/phases/2/question: 随流亡白党武力还乡吗？
events/1308_inferno/phases/2/options/0/r: 1304 年 7 月 20 日，拉斯特拉。流亡白党联军兵败如山倒，尸横遍野。你若在场，已经死了。——再想想。
events/1308_inferno/phases/2/options/1/r:
你们的仇恨和他们的仇恨，是同一种东西。
与其与愚人同行——我自成一党（parte per te stesso）。
events/1308_inferno/phases/2/conclusion/: 1304 年拉斯特拉惨败后，但丁与流亡白党彻底决裂，从此「自成一党」。他失去了最后一个阵营——也第一次真正自由了。没有党派可以代言的人，只能对全人类说话。
events/1308_inferno/phases/3/sin/did:
他们生前收钱替人看未来：谁会赢，谁该死，哪一天该出兵。
有人真信，有人骗人。但丁要把他们放进地狱——罚，得由他来定。
events/1308_inferno/phases/3/question: 如果由你来写这一段，你要把他们改成什么样？
events/1308_inferno/phases/3/parts/3/tex: 变成一尊不会动的石像
events/1308_inferno/phases/3/danteVersio:
他们的头被拧向后面，脸朝着脊背。想往前走，就只能倒着走——因为他们再也看不见前面。
眼泪顺着后背往下淌。（《地狱》第二十歌）
events/1308_inferno/phases/3/mirror/puni: 死后：永远只看得见后面
events/1308_inferno/phases/3/rule:
罪的形状，翻过来，就是罚的形状。
但丁给这个规矩起了名字：contrapasso。

看懂这条规矩，你就能自己推剩下的八圈了——这也正是接下来要做的事。
events/1308_inferno/phases/4/transitionT:
《地狱》一歌一歌地写着，在各个宫廷之间传抄。
1308 年深秋，一名信使闯进廊下——
events/1308_inferno/phases/4/announcemen:
「由我进入愁苦之城，
由我进入永劫之苦，
由我进入沉沦之民中间。

进来的人，把一切希望留在门外。」
quiz/1308_inferno/quizzes/0/question: 但丁决定用哪种语言写《神曲》？
quiz/1308_inferno/quizzes/0/options/0: 拉丁文——学术与教会的正统语言
quiz/1308_inferno/quizzes/0/options/1: 法语——宫廷文学的通行语言
quiz/1308_inferno/quizzes/0/options/2: 意大利俗语——「让面包坊的女工也能读懂的语言」
quiz/1308_inferno/quizzes/0/options/3: 希腊语——古典史诗的语言
quiz/1308_inferno/quizzes/0/explanation: 但丁在《论俗语》中为母语辩护，并用托斯卡纳俗语写成《神曲》——这一文学史级别的决定让「俗语」升格为文学语言，他因此被称为「意大利语之父」。
quiz/1308_inferno/quizzes/1/question: 但丁说「我自成一党」（parte per te stesso），指的是什么？
quiz/1308_inferno/quizzes/1/options/1: 他拒绝随流亡白党联合吉伯林党武力还乡，与他们决裂
quiz/1308_inferno/quizzes/1/explanation: 流亡白党勾结吉伯林党武力还乡，1304 年拉斯特拉一役惨败。但丁拒绝参与并与之决裂——「自成一党」。从此他不再属于任何阵营，只对全人类说话。
quiz/1308_inferno/quizzes/2/question:
《地狱》第三歌，地狱之门铭文的最后一行：
「入此门者，当舍弃一切___」
quiz/1308_inferno/quizzes/2/explanation: 「Lasciate ogne speranza, voi ch'intrate」——入此门者，当舍弃一切希望。但丁把流亡最深处的绝望，刻在了《地狱》的门楣上；然后他推门进去，开始写。
events/1313_impero/phases/0/transitionTe: 讲坛上，薄伽丘展开三封信的抄件。
events/1313_impero/phases/0/announcement: 薄伽丘：「一生最后一次政治豪赌。他把全部的赌注——包括回家的可能——都押在一个德意志人身上。诸位看他怎么下注。」
events/1313_impero/phases/1/narrative: 亨利七世率军翻过阿尔卑斯山。流亡者的书案上，三封公开信陆续写就，摊在案上。
events/1313_impero/phases/1/instruction: 读完三封信，再听听抄写员怎么说。
events/1313_impero/phases/1/npcs/0/name: 信一 · 致意大利诸侯
events/1313_impero/phases/1/npcs/0/dialo: 「看哪，现在是蒙恩的时候！新郎来了，意大利的新娘，擦干你的眼泪——罗马的皇帝来做万民的和平了！」
events/1313_impero/phases/1/npcs/1/dialo: 「你们这些愚妄之徒！僭越一切神法与人法，贪婪驱使你们无恶不作——城墙救不了你们，鹰旗之下，你们必将颤抖！」
（笔锋未停）骂痛快了。也把自己钉死在流亡名单上了。
events/1313_impero/phases/1/npcs/2/dialo: 「你为何迁延？你在米兰过冬，以为托斯卡纳不足虑？错了！先诛佛罗伦萨——这条毒蛇，这只病羊，它正在污染整个羊群！」
events/1313_impero/phases/1/npcs/3/dialo: （手抖）先生，这些信……骂的是您自己的故乡。
一旦寄出，传遍诸城——佛罗伦萨永远、永远不会赦免您了。
events/1313_impero/phases/2/narrative: 抄写员捧着信，等最后一句话。
events/1313_impero/phases/2/options/0/re: 他没有缓。历史不给这个选项——你面前的这个人，从不给自己留退路。
events/1313_impero/phases/2/options/1/re:
正义在此一举。
寄出去——让全意大利听见。
events/1313_impero/phases/2/conclusion/n: 三封信传遍意大利。佛罗伦萨的回应是把但丁永远排除在任何赦免之外。他押上了回家的路，去赌一个帝国的梦。
events/1313_impero/phases/3/travelNarrat: 亨利七世翻越阿尔卑斯山南下。情绪从沸点，一站一站冷下去。
events/1313_impero/phases/3/instruction: 沿鹰旗的路线，点击每一站。
events/1313_impero/phases/3/waypoints/0/: 圣安布罗焦教堂，亨利戴上伦巴第的铁王冠。观礼的人群里，一个流亡的诗人挤到御前——俯身，吻了皇帝的脚。
我见到了他。正义的化身，活的。二十年了，我第一次觉得离家这么近。
events/1313_impero/phases/3/waypoints/1/: 布雷西亚闭门抗拒。围城四个月，疫病横行，联军开始瓦解。贵尔夫诸城冷眼旁观——那不勒斯的罗贝托王已在集结军队。
events/1313_impero/phases/3/waypoints/2/: 罗马巷战。圣彼得堂被敌军占据，加冕只能改在拉特兰教堂——一场残缺的加冕。教皇远在阿维尼翁，连使节都显得敷衍。
皇冠戴上了，可圣彼得的门是关着的。……不祥。
events/1313_impero/phases/3/waypoints/3/: 大军再度南征。8 月 24 日，锡耶纳附近的小镇布翁孔文托——
events/1313_impero/phases/4/transitionTe:
灵帐前，鹰旗倒卷。
亨利死后，但丁再未对现世政治抱任何希望。
他把皇帝写进了《天堂》。

讲坛上，薄伽丘停了很久。
events/1313_impero/phases/4/announcement: 薄伽丘：「他赌输了。可诸位——正因为人间的宝座空了，他才把整座天堂修成了法庭。《神曲》的裁决，比任何皇帝的都长久。」
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/0/question: 1310–1313 年，但丁把最后的政治希望押在谁身上？
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/0/options/2: 神圣罗马皇帝亨利七世
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/0/explanation: 亨利七世南下意大利，但丁连写公开信劝诸侯迎驾、骂佛罗伦萨、催亨利先打佛罗伦萨——言辞激烈到断送了自己被赦免的一切可能。1313 年亨利暴病死于布翁孔文托，梦碎。
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/1/question: 但丁用什么比喻反驳教廷的「日月说」、主张政教并立？
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/1/explanation: 教廷主张「日月说」——皇权像月亮，只能借教皇太阳的光。但丁针锋相对提出「两个太阳」（比喻见《炼狱》第十六歌）：帝国与教会各自直接受命于神。《帝制论》系统论证此说，后被教会列为禁书焚毁。
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/2/question:
《天堂》第三十歌，至高玫瑰的座席中：
「有一把空椅，上面放着一顶___，等着高贵的亨利」
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/2/explanation: 《天堂》XXX：贝雅特丽切指给但丁看天堂玫瑰中的空座与王冠——人间容不下的皇帝，天堂给他留了座。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/0/narrative: 流亡第十三年。佛罗伦萨颁布大赦令——一封信送到了客居的小院。快五十岁的但丁，想家想了十三年。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/0/instructio: 读完大赦令的条款，再听听身边人的话。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/0/npcs/0/dia: 阿利吉耶里先生，好消息！城里大赦流亡者。条件念给您听——
「其一，缴纳罚金。其二，着悔罪服，头戴纸帽。其三，随游街队伍至圣乔万尼洗礼堂，向主保圣人献祭赎罪。」
走完这一遭，就能回家了。先生，多少人求都求不来啊。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/0/npcs/1/dia: 羊皮纸上是熟悉的公社印鉴。「悔罪」「献祭」几个词，写得格外端正。
圣乔万尼洗礼堂……我受洗的地方。他们要我以罪人的身份，游街回到我人生开始的地方。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/0/npcs/2/dia: 先生，爷爷说您天天朝南边看。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/0/npcs/3/dia: 父亲。判决株连诸子——我和雅各波，也在流亡名单上。
认了吧。纸帽子戴一天就摘了。我想回家。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/1/situation:
十三年后，佛罗伦萨来信：
缴罚金、穿悔罪服、由人押着游街认罪——就放你回来。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/1/options/0/: 接受。缴罚金、游街、回家——妻儿团聚，落叶归根。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/1/options/1/: 拒绝。宁可老死在别人的屋檐下。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/1/sameNote: 你猜对了。那接着问一句：他凭什么觉得这值得？
events/1315_amnistia/phases/1/diffNote: 他没有接。十三年了，唯一一次回家的机会，他没有接。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/1/reveal:
「这不是我返乡的路。
若另有一条不损但丁名誉与尊严的路，我会毫不迟疑地走上去。
若没有——那我永不踏进佛罗伦萨。

难道我在别处，就看不见日月星辰吗？
难道不先在故乡自辱一场，我就想不了最甜的道理吗？
面包，哪里都不会缺。」
——《书信》第十二
events/1315_amnistia/phases/1/consequenc:
几个月后，佛罗伦萨改了判决：但丁及诸子，斩首。（此前是火刑。）

他再没回去。1321 年死在拉文纳，葬在那里。
此后六百年，佛罗伦萨一次又一次向拉文纳讨他的骨殖，一次也没讨到。
圣十字教堂里给他修的那座墓，至今是空的。
events/1315_amnistia/phases/2/transition:
数月后，佛罗伦萨改判：
但丁及诸子，斩首。
（此前为火刑。）
events/1315_amnistia/phases/2/announceme: 薄伽丘合上讲义，沉默良久：「诸位同乡。我们的城把最好的儿子拒之门外两次——第一次用火刑，第二次用纸帽子。而他用一整部《天堂》回答：他只接受一种加冕。若有朝一日《神曲》让他返乡，他愿在自己受洗的池边，戴上桂冠。」
events/1315_amnistia/phases/2/dufu_react:
「若这圣诗能战胜将我拒于羊栏之外的残忍——
我将以另一种嗓音、另一身羊毛归来，
在我受洗的池边，接受桂冠。」（《天堂》XXV）
quiz/1315_amnistia/quizzes/0/question: 1315 年佛罗伦萨大赦，要求流亡者以什么条件换取回城？
quiz/1315_amnistia/quizzes/0/options/1: 缴罚金、穿悔罪服戴纸帽游街、到洗礼堂献祭赎罪
quiz/1315_amnistia/quizzes/0/explanation: 大赦条件是缴纳罚金、着悔罪服头戴纸帽随游街队伍至圣乔万尼洗礼堂「献祭」——以罪人身份公开受辱。但丁在《书信》XII 中回答：「这不是我返乡之路。」
quiz/1315_amnistia/quizzes/1/question: 但丁拒绝大赦后，佛罗伦萨对他的判决改为？
quiz/1315_amnistia/quizzes/1/options/2: 但丁及诸子斩首（此前为火刑）
quiz/1315_amnistia/quizzes/1/explanation: 拒绝大赦数月后，佛罗伦萨改判但丁及诸子斩首——株连到儿子们。而他早已在拒绝信里写下了答案：「面包，哪里都不会缺。」
quiz/1315_amnistia/quizzes/2/question:
《天堂》第二十五歌开篇，但丁写下唯一接受的加冕方式：
「我将以另一种嗓音、另一身羊毛归来，在我受洗的池边，接受___」
quiz/1315_amnistia/quizzes/2/explanation: 《天堂》XXV：「若这圣诗能战胜将我拒于羊栏之外的残忍……我将在受洗的池边接受桂冠。」呼应 1265 年他受洗的圣乔万尼洗礼堂——他至死没有等到，佛罗伦萨至今欠他这顶桂冠。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/0/transitionT:
圣斯特凡诺教堂。烛火比往常多点了一倍。
薄伽丘翻开讲义的最后一册。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/0/announcemen: 薄伽丘：「故事讲到头了。一座海边的城收留了他——拉文纳。诸位会看到：一个失去一切的人，怎样把一切写完。」
events/1321_ravenna/phases/1/narrative: 1318 年前后，拉文纳领主圭多·诺韦洛·达·波伦塔遣使相邀。海松林沙沙作响，子女前来团聚——流亡的最后一站，竟像个家。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/1/instruction: 在松林与宫廷之间走走，见见这里的人。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/1/npcs/0/dial: 先生肯来，是拉文纳之幸。宅子备好了，束脩从优——不，不是门客。是先生。
我也写诗。改日……可否请先生斧正？（领主执弟子礼。）
events/1321_ravenna/phases/1/npcs/1/dial: 父亲。我在城里的圣斯特凡诺修院做了修女。
我的法号——贝雅特丽切修女。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/1/npcs/2/dial: 《地狱》《炼狱》的抄本，各城都在传。先生——《天堂》还差最后几歌。
写完它。全意大利都在等。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/2/narrative: 圣阿波利纳雷教堂。六世纪的金色马赛克，已经燃烧了八百年。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/2/instruction: 点击教堂里打动他的东西。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/2/npcs/0/dial: 金箔嵌片在烛光里明明灭灭，像凝固的光的海洋。圣徒们立在永恒的金色里。
金色的穹顶……天堂的光，原来人间见过。
（《天堂》篇里那些光的漩涡、光的玫瑰、光的河流——视觉的底稿，就在拉文纳的穹顶上。）
events/1321_ravenna/phases/2/npcs/1/dial: 博洛尼亚的学者乔万尼·德尔·维吉利奥来信：「用俗语写传世之作，可惜了。改用拉丁文重写吧，我为你在博洛尼亚谋桂冠。」
（提笔，以拉丁牧歌体回赠了他两首田园诗——诗艺无可挑剔，答案只有一个字：不。）
面包坊的女工读不懂拉丁文。俗语的胜利，就差最后十三歌了。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/3/transitionT:
1321 年夏，拉文纳与威尼斯起了争端。
但丁为圭多出使威尼斯斡旋，归途取道沼泽水路——
蚊虫，热病。疟疾。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/3/announcemen: 五十六岁的但丁·阿利吉耶里，在拉文纳去世。子女守在榻前。《天堂》的最后十三歌，遍寻书房——无人找到。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/3/dufu_reacti:
面包，哪里都不会缺……
只是《天堂》……还差十三歌。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/narrative: 八个月后。一个流传至今的传说——
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/panels/0/di: 儿子雅各波梦中见父。白衣，微笑，周身有光。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/panels/1/di: 「你要找的东西，」父亲抬手，指向生前卧室的墙壁，「在那里。」
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/panels/2/di: 掀开壁毯——墙上有一个小壁龛，里面是一叠受潮发霉的手稿。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/panels/3/di: 拂去霉斑，字迹尚可辨认——正是《天堂》的最后十三歌。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/panels/4/di: 最后一页 · 最后一行

l'amor che move il sole e l'altre stelle——
是爱，推动太阳与群星。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/rule: 但丁的宇宙：地在正中，九重天裹在外面。越往外，转得越快——因为离神越近。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/0/n: 皮卡尔达在这里。她被亲哥哥从修道院里拖出去逼嫁——誓是别人替她破的，可她还是只能停在最低的一重。她说：在这里我是满足的。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/1/h: 做了好事、但也图个名声的人
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/1/n: 查士丁尼皇帝在这里，替罗马法说话。行善掺了一点求名的心，就上不去更高。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/2/n: 他们生前的爱越了界，死后仍在爱，只是这一次爱对了方向。但丁没有因为「多情」就把人往下放。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/3/n: 十二位智者围成一圈转，托马斯·阿奎那在里面。有意思的是：阿奎那在这里替一个和他吵了一辈子的对手说好话。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/4/n: 众灵排成一个巨大的十字。卡恰圭达从十字上下来认他这个后代——也是在这里，他对但丁说了那句「别人的面包多咸」。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/5/n: 众灵先排成一行字，再变成一只鹰。这只鹰会说话，而且它说的是「我们」——公正不是一个人的事。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/6/n: 一架金梯从这里往上，看不见顶。这一重安静得反常——但丁说，再往上贝雅特丽切就不能对他笑了，笑会烧坏他。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/7/n: 圣彼得考「信」，圣雅各考「望」，圣约翰考「爱」。人间那场制举他没考上，这一场他答完了。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/8/h: 推动其余一切的那一重
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/8/n: 这里没有实体，只有九级天使围着一个极亮的点转。整个宇宙的时间从这一重开始走。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/finale/line: 你从一座幽暗森林出发。
穿过地狱，爬上炼狱山，走进了群星。
一路上遇见的人，一个也没有凭空出现——
他们都是但丁在佛罗伦萨认识过的人。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/finale/coda:
全诗的最后一行写的是：
是爱，在推动太阳和其他的星辰。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/6/transitionT: 薄伽丘合上讲义。教堂里很静。
events/1321_ravenna/phases/6/announcemen: 薄伽丘：「这是传说。但《天堂》确实是完整的——这才是奇迹本身。1373 年的今天，佛罗伦萨付钱请我讲但丁；拉文纳至今不肯归还他的遗骨。他说过的：面包，哪里都不会缺。安息吧，诗人。这部《喜剧》，请允许我们后人擅自替它加一个字——神圣的（Divina）。」
quiz/1321_ravenna/quizzes/0/question: 《天堂》第二十四至二十六歌，三位使徒分别考但丁什么？
quiz/1321_ravenna/quizzes/0/explanation: 圣彼得考「信」、圣雅各考「望」、圣约翰考「爱」。但丁全部通过，圣彼得绕他三匝如光环流转——与 747 年杜甫遭遇的人间作弊的制举遥相呼应：这场考试，天堂公正。

quiz/1321_ravenna/quizzes/2/question:
《神曲》的最后一行：
「是爱，推动太阳与___」
quiz/1321_ravenna/quizzes/2/explanation: 「l'amor che move il sole e l'altre stelle」——是爱，推动太阳与群星。《地狱》《炼狱》《天堂》三部的最后一个词都是「群星」（stelle）。
